title: 2023 year-end financial results and police budget questions
subtitle: Q1 2024 plan update, CFO Craig Dyer's retirement, election sign by-law review and honorarium policy requests
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council approve the preliminary 2023 financial results so the Region's 2023 audited financial statements can be prepared, and that the Surplus Allocation Policy be applied to those results {{vote:m2}}. The motion had been deferred from April 24 so that councillors could review questions put to the Waterloo Regional Police Service Board and its responses.

The committee received the Q1 2024 Plan and Financial Update for information. The acting Chief Administrative Officer said the Region is on track with no major financial flags, and noted positive provincial and federal funding announcements. Several police-related reports and correspondence items were also received for information. Regional Chair Karen Redman marked the upcoming retirement of Craig Dyer, Chief Financial Officer, after 12 years with the Region.

Under other business, one councillor asked staff to look at rescinding the current election sign by-law and returning to the previous one. Staff are to circulate the earlier by-law, and a notice of motion would follow. Another councillor asked staff for information on honorariums for standing committee chairs. These are requests for staff work, not decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the preliminary 2023 financial results for preparing the Region's 2023 audited financial statements {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended applying the Surplus Allocation Policy to the 2023 financial results, as part of the same motion {{vote:m2}}.

debate: One councillor said the police board chair's response to their budget questions was inappropriate and attacked their character, and argued that councillors asking questions on behalf of taxpayers should not be treated that way. The same councillor still supported passing the motion so the matter could move to the next step.

Another councillor said the exchange harms the police service's standing in the community, noting that the questions had been answered and rebuttals exchanged. They suggested the new Police Act's inspector general as a route for future disputes and raised concern about difficulty recruiting officers. The chair asked them to keep to the year-end results motion.

On the election sign by-law, the councillor raising it said signs serve a purpose, including visibility that may encourage voting, and wanted the previous by-law reviewed. Another councillor asked whether the public would have input, and staff were expected to bring a report with an opportunity for delegations.

A further councillor doubted that signs would raise turnout and suggested hearing from a political scientist on why people do not vote in municipal elections. Another said they were working with a university researcher on a possible citizens' assembly on municipal elections.
